title: the DMZ Rising
premise: Orsen Galloway, a private security contractor protecting a disgraced intelligence broker named Vera Kade, discovers their remote safe house listed for sale online — with interior photos that reveal hidden documents he was never supposed to know existed. The listing is bait, set by the syndicate that once employed him, and the only way to protect Vera is to trade the secret she's been hoarding: proof of who ordered a massacre five years ago that Orsen's dead brother was blamed for. As the syndicate closes in and Orsen's own agency sells him out, he learns the massacre was ordered by the man who trained him, and that Vera has known all along. In the end, Orsen trades the secret publicly — burning his career and Vera's leverage — to expose the truth, choosing loyalty to his brother's memory over the woman he's come to love.
about_author: Lior Zhou is a former risk consultant who spent a decade advising security firms across three continents before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about the people paid to keep secrets they never agreed to carry.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. During a routine supply run, Orsen finds the safe house — his safe house — listed on a real estate site with photos of the interior, including the sealed basement door. The emotional beat is cold dread: someone has been inside, and the agency's response is to deny everything.

chapters.title: House Rules
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He returns to find Vera Kade calm, almost pleased, insisting the listing is a negotiation ploy by her old handlers. Flashbacks reveal five years of isolation and the growing intimacy between them. Emotional beat: uneasy trust fraying at the edges.

chapters.title: Basement Light
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Alone, Vera opens the basement and we see what she guards: a ledger naming who ordered the Halloway Bridge massacre. She photographs one page and hides the original. Emotional beat: guilt — she's been using Orsen as a lock, not a partner.

chapters.title: The Broker's Client
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. His agency handler, Marsh, orders him to extract Vera to a new site in 72 hours — suspiciously fast. Orsen notices the extraction route passes through syndicate territory. Emotional beat: the first crack in his loyalty to the agency.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A couple tours the property — actually syndicate scouts mapping defenses. Orsen runs them off but realizes the listing was a probe to learn how many guards remain. Emotional beat: hunted, and understanding he always was.

chapters.title: What Vera Knew
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera recalls the day she bought the ledger and the day she learned her new bodyguard was the massacre scapegoat's brother — and hired him anyway, half penance, half shield. Emotional beat: love entangled with calculation.

chapters.title: Dead Drop Protocol
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Marsh's extraction team arrives early and armed. Orsen stalls them, and in the confusion a team member whispers that Orsen's brother's file was sealed by someone still serving. Emotional beat: betrayal sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. The syndicate's negotiator, Ilsa Renner, contacts Vera directly: the ledger for safe passage out of the country. Vera pretends to consider, buying time, but Renner reveals she knows Orsen's identity. Emotional beat: Vera's protective lie begins to collapse.

chapters.title: Brother's Keeper
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen confronts Vera about his brother; she admits the ledger names his killer but refuses to show it, claiming it's the only thing keeping them both alive. Emotional beat: love against duty, first open rupture.

chapters.title: Severance
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The agency formally cuts Orsen loose — his credentials die mid-transit, and a kill order is issued under his own name. He realizes Marsh authored the listing to force the ledger into the open. Emotional beat: orphaned, furious, free.

chapters.title: Renner's Offer
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Renner corners Vera with a better offer: the ledger for Orsen's life. Vera, who has spent five years trading other people's secrets, must decide what hers are worth. Emotional beat: the cost of love made explicit.

chapters.title: Night Run
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen moves Vera to a fallback cabin through a storm, evading both syndicate and agency teams. Wounded, feverish, he confesses he'd trade the ledger for his brother's name even if it kills her. Emotional beat: honesty as intimacy, at last.

chapters.title: The Third Copy
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera reveals there were always three copies — one with her, one she suspects Marsh already has, and one hidden in the safe house itself, which explains the listing. Emotional beat: hope that the trap can be reversed.

chapters.title: Return to the House
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. They go back for the third copy and find the safe house staged for a showing — syndicate cleaners stripping it. Orsen retrieves the copy from a hidden floor cavity seconds before discovery. Emotional beat: claustrophobic suspense, narrow escape.

chapters.title: Marsh's Confession
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen ambushes Marsh, who admits the agency ordered the massacre and used Orsen's brother as the fall guy — and that the ledger was the agency's own insurance, stolen by Vera. Emotional beat: the mentor unmasked; grief curdles into resolve.

chapters.title: Vera's Choice
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Renner gives a final deadline. Vera prepares to trade the ledger for passage, then finds Orsen's brother's name annotated in her own handwriting from years ago — she'd known the killer's name before she ever met him. Emotional beat: shame, and the decision to stop managing the truth.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. At a border rail yard, the trade goes forward — but Orsen substitutes a partial copy, keeping the page naming the orderer. Renner's team detects the swap; a firefight erupts. Emotional beat: the gamble that costs everything but the truth.

chapters.title: Ash and Ledger
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Wounded, Vera chooses to broadcast the full ledger rather than trade it, uploading it to a dead-man's-switch network as Renner closes in. Emotional beat: duty finally aligned with love — she protects Orsen with the truth.

chapters.title: Halloway Bridge
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The ledger goes public. The orderer — the agency's founding director — is named, and Marsh is arrested trying to contain it. Orsen stands at the bridge where his brother died. Emotional beat: vindication that feels like loss.

chapters.title: What the Secret Bought
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera surrenders to prosecutors, trading testimony for leniency, and refuses Orsen's plan to run. She tells him love built on a hidden ledger was never love. Emotional beat: bittersweet separation with the door left open.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Months later, Orsen testifies at the inquiry, finally saying his brother's name on the record. The agency is dismantled; Renner vanishes with the syndicate's remnants. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning, the weight set down.

chapters.title: The House on the Market
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen buys the safe house at auction — the listing that started it all — and finds Vera waiting on the porch, out on parole, no secrets left between them. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed; a beginning, not an ending.
